name: 55-91 dominoes

history.origins: Block/draw dominoes with double-9 (55 tiles) to double-12 (91 tiles). Same matching rules; set size and player count vary.
timeline: 12th–13th century: Chinese domino tiles used in gambling games and playing-card style games.
Mid-18th century: modern Western block and draw domino games using extended sets documented in France and spreading across Europe and North America.
history.cultural: Domino games; larger sets for more players.

setup.players: 2-6 players depending on domino set size.
setup.dealing: Draw tiles; the number per player depends on set size and player count, with any remainder forming a boneyard in draw games.
setup.equipment: Domino set and a playing surface or table.

rules.objective: Play all tiles first, or have fewest pips if blocked.
rules.gameplay: Highest double leads. Match one number to an open end; doubles crosswise. Block: pass if cannot play. Draw: draw from boneyard until playable. Winner scores opponents' pips or lowest hand if blocked.
keyRules: Match to open ends; doubles crosswise

strategy.basic: Match tile ends; block or draw per variant; go out to win.
strategy.intermediate: Track high tiles; force opponents to draw in draw games.
strategy.advanced: Suit count; endgame planning for multiple set sizes.
tips: Same matching rules across set sizes; player count varies.
